headline: THE BOUNDARY IS SMALLER AND MORE CONCENTRATED THAN THE RECORD IMPLIES. There is **no literal 'studio' or 'marketing' coupling anywhere in the runtime path** — a grep over autornd/** returns one hit, in a docstring explaining why vocabularies are open. Everything domain-specific arrives through the profile or the scenario. What remains hardcoded is **one vocabulary of roles and two rules that reach into it**, plus **seven prompt strings that say 'engineering' out loud**.

questions_for_advisor: **The survey's headline is that B14 is smaller than staged.** §26 framed it as 'two literal engineering roles bind on every profile', with the measured impact that 77 of 108 units got a test engineer. That is real — but the generalization is TWO PROFILE KEYS, not an architecture. The rules themselves (scale the review team with risk; someone checks the work; someone holds the system view) are already domain-neutral. Only their operands are engineering nouns.

**And smartfactory cannot validate it.** Its manifest's domains are firmware, hardware, backend, frontend, infrastructure — five shipped enum members. It is an engineering project and would run today. If Blueprint 017 wants live validation of the boundary, it needs a non-engineering corpus, and the only one in the tree is the studio profile with no documents behind it. That is a gap worth closing before the blueprint is written, not after.

**§26's line references have drifted and one was always incomplete.** review_composition.py's recorded 53-60 covers two of four reaches; the constants at 17-18 are outside it. A blueprint written from the recorded reference would generalize half the site and measure a partial fix. Re-stated at HEAD above — and this is the argument for the blueprint citing symbols rather than lines.
public_safe_summary: Read-only survey of B14's design inputs, no spend. The boundary is smaller and more concentrated than the record implies: there is no literal studio or marketing coupling anywhere in the runtime path, and what remains is one role vocabulary plus three rules that reach into it, one workflow file naming two roles as data, and seven prompt strings saying 'engineering'. The recorded line references for both named boundary sites have drifted, and one always understated its site by half. The largest finding is that docs/smartfactory is an engineering project — its manifest's domains are all shipped enum members — so it cannot validate the generalization boundary; it would run on today's path unchanged.
next_recommended_commands: Blueprint 017, with a non-engineering corpus named for its live validation.
